def: The passage of a document that is embedded, indexed, retrieved and cited as one unit.
Repeating the last words of one chunk at the start of the next so facts near a boundary appear whole somewhere, at the cost of extra storage.
Splitting a document along its own divisions such as sections, clauses, slides or functions instead of at fixed lengths.
Cutting where the embedding similarity between neighbouring sentences drops, so chunk size follows topic changes.
A short self-contained statement, with pronouns resolved, extracted from a passage and used as a fine-grained retrieval unit.
A chunk that has lost the context needed to interpret it, such as which company, section or quarter it refers to.
Prepending a short generated or derived context to each chunk before it is embedded and indexed, so the chunk can be found by what it is about.
Encoding a whole document with a long-context embedder first and pooling token embeddings into chunk vectors afterwards, so each chunk vector sees its surroundings.
Matching small child chunks in the index but returning the larger parent passage that contains them, also called small-to-big retrieval.
Storing the processed form of a repeated prompt prefix so later requests that reuse it are cheaper and faster.
The share of questions for which at least one of the top k returned chunks contains the answer.
